---
name: qinyang-design
description: Design rules, limits and checks for interfaces built with qinyang/ui (the @qinyang shadcn registry). Use when building, reviewing or restyling any screen, component, block or template on it, when writing UI copy or registry descriptions, when picking colours, radii, type, icons, charts or motion, and before committing UI changes (run the check script).
---

# qinyang/ui design

qinyang/ui is a desktop-density component library: a 13px type scale, translucent fills on opaque
surfaces, alpha hairlines, four elevation levels, corners that derive from one `--radius` and stop at
16px, one accent swapped through eight role tokens. These rules keep every screen and every coding
agent on that one style. Each rule is a short instruction, the reason, and what to write; the
references hold the exact values.

## Install

```bash
npx skills add QinYangWang/ui --skill qinyang-design
```

The library itself installs with the shadcn CLI (`npx shadcn@latest add @qinyang/theme`, then any
item). See `references/registry.md`.

## Check

```bash
node .agents/skills/qinyang-design/scripts/check.mjs            # wherever the skill was installed
node .agents/skills/qinyang-design/scripts/check.mjs app src    # only these paths
```

Static checks for most of the rules below (tokens, radius cap and concentric nesting, type scale,
tracking, press scale, transitions, icon imports, menu labels, copy density, provenance, registry
names, stale theme). No dependencies; with TypeScript in the project it reads JSX exactly (the native
TypeScript 7 compiler has no parser API, so there it falls back to line checks). Exit code 1
on errors (`--strict`: warnings too), `--json` for tools, `--list` for the rule ids. Configure it in
`qinyang-design.config.json` (allow-list a file with a reason, add names that must not appear in copy);
silence one line with a comment `design-check-ignore <rule> -- <reason>` above it.

Nested radii also need a runtime look: open the screen in a browser (menus open, a row hovered) and
paste `scripts/radius-probe.js` into the console. It lists every rounded element more than 2px off
concentric. Run the check before you commit and fix what it reports; a finding you keep gets an
allow-list entry with its reason.

## Rules

### 1. Colour with theme tokens

Tokens follow the theme, the accent preset and dark mode; palette classes and hex values don't.

Use `bg-card`, `text-muted-foreground`, `bg-success-subtle`, `inset-ring-success-border`, `var(--chart-3)`.
Never `bg-zinc-100`, `text-green-600`, `[#0090ff]` or a hex in a component. `white`/`black` only for scrims.

### 2. Put text on a solid in its foreground token

The neutral accent's solid is near-white in dark mode, so `text-white` disappears on it.

`bg-primary text-primary-foreground`, `bg-destructive text-destructive-foreground`. Hover a filled
control to `bg-primary-hover`, press to `bg-primary-active`, never `/90`.

### 3. Fill for state, surface for panels

`secondary`, `muted` and `accent` are translucent fills; anything that floats or holds content needs an opaque surface.

Hover, selected and track fills use `bg-secondary` / `bg-accent` / `bg-foreground/6`. Cards, popovers,
menus and dialogs use `bg-card`, `bg-popover` or `bg-background`.

### 4. Elevate with shadow tokens, not borders plus shadows

Each shadow level already carries its own hairline, so a CSS border on top doubles the edge.

`shadow-raised` for resting cards, tables, code and controls, `shadow-surface` for popovers and menus,
`shadow-xl` for dialogs, drawers and the command palette, `shadow-well` for fields and tracks, `shadow-chip`
for keys and small chips. Dividers inside a surface are `border-border` (an alpha hairline).

### 5. Keep series on the chart palette

Eight fixed hues read the same under every accent, in both modes, and keep neighbours apart.

Series are `var(--chart-1)` … `var(--chart-8)` in order; status colours only where the colour means a
status. Never `primary` in a chart. Legend and tooltip swatches are round dots.

### 6. Keep nested radii concentric

A child corner that doesn't follow its container's curve reads as a mistake at every radius preset.

Inner radius = outer radius − padding. Put `frame-{token} frame-p-{n}` on the container and
`rounded-inner` on the child; a padded child that holds more rows takes `frame-inner`, never
`frame-inner` and `rounded-inner` together. Insets of 8px or less are always concentric.

### 7. Stay at or under 16px

Past 16px containers turn into blobs and nested parts can't stay concentric.

Use `rounded-sm` … `rounded-3xl`; every token clamps at `--radius-max`. Never `rounded-4xl`/`5xl` in new
code or an arbitrary radius above 1rem. `rounded-full` only for round things: avatars, dots, switches,
slider thumbs, badges and tags, icon-only circular buttons, progress bars.

### 8. Derive every radius from the base radius

Presets and the radius slider rescale `--radius` and the tokens built on it, never literal pixel radii.

Use a token, or `rounded-[calc(var(--radius)*k)]` (clamped with `min(…, var(--radius-max))` above 2×).
Only 1–2px caret radii, `rounded-full` and `rounded-[inherit]` stay literal.

### 9. Use the UI type scale

One compact scale keeps dense screens even; arbitrary sizes drift.

Components use `text-ui-2xs` 10 · `text-ui-xs` 11 · `text-ui-sm` 12 · `text-ui` 13 · `text-ui-lg` 14.
Reading copy and page headings use `text-sm` and up; `text-3xl`+ only for heroes. Never `text-[11px]`.

### 10. Semibold titles, medium labels

Two weights carry the hierarchy; heavier text shouts in a dense layout.

Titles `font-semibold`, labels and buttons `font-medium`, body `font-normal`. `font-bold` only in
reading copy that needs it.

### 11. Keep the font's tracking

The type is spaced for its size; tightening small text makes it harder to read.

`tracking-tight` only from `text-xl` up. Wide tracking only on uppercase labels and shortcut glyphs.

### 12. Use tabular numbers for numbers that change or align

Proportional digits make columns and counters jump.

`tabular-nums` on prices, timers, tickers, table columns and counts. `text-balance` on headings,
`text-pretty` on paragraphs.

### 13. Size controls for desktop density

Desktop screens hold more per view; touch-sized controls waste it.

Buttons and inputs `h-8` (sm `h-7`, xs `h-6`, lg `h-9`), menu rows 26px, sidebar rows `h-8` (sub rows
`h-7`), checkbox 16px, switch 32×20, disabled `opacity-64`. Use component sizes, not heights.

### 14. Space related things closer

Spacing groups content before any border does.

4px grid. Icon + label `gap-1.5`–`gap-2`, control groups `gap-2`–`gap-3`, card padding `p-4`–`p-6`,
sections `gap-6`–`gap-10`. Put space with `gap` on the parent, never padding on a component.

### 15. Start navigation text on one left edge

Indents and guide lines widen the sidebar and break the column the eye follows.

Section labels, group labels and rows share one text edge; hierarchy comes from type and spacing.
The active row is a fill (`bg-secondary` or `bg-foreground/6`) with an optional 2px bar in the gutter.

### 16. Compose the library, don't restyle it

A component's variants and sizes are its design; overriding them per screen forks the style.

Pick a `variant`/`size`; `className` on a component is for layout (margins, `w-full`, grid placement).
If nothing fits, style a plain wrapper, or add a variant to the component in its own change.

### 17. Keep a menu label inside its group

The label names the group for assistive tech, and the primitive label throws outside one.

`<MenuGroup><MenuLabel>Agent</MenuLabel>…items…</MenuGroup>`; the same for select and combobox labels.

### 18. Chevrons for folders, file icons for files

A folder icon next to a chevron says the same thing twice and pushes names apart.

Folders show only the expand chevron; files show their file-type icon in the same column, so names
at one level line up.

### 19. Draw icons from one family per group

Two glyph families in one group look like two different products.

Navigation, rails, docks, tab bars and palettes use the solid family (`InboxIcon`, `CalendarDaysIcon`,
`TerminalSquareIcon`); line glyphs are for controls (chevrons, close, add, search). Icons come from
`@/components/icons` only, 16px and muted in navigation.

### 20. Frame title icons, keep nav icons bare

A frame marks an icon as the subject of a card; in a list it is clutter.

Card, alert and header icons sit in `<IconChip>` (one size per list, tone for status). Nav, toolbar
and inline icons are bare and take their size from the control.

### 21. Use real brand marks for other products

Redrawn or approximated logos look wrong to anyone who knows the brand.

`<BrandIcon icon={siGithub} />` with one named import per logo; `color="brand"` where the logo is the
content, the default `current` in toolbars and nav. Brands the set leaves out get a neutral icon.

### 22. Show people and workspaces as avatars

An avatar says "who"; a generic icon in that spot says nothing.

`<Avatar>` with an image, a generated face or initials, round for people, `shape="rounded"` for workspaces
and teams.

### 23. Answer a press with a fill

Native controls don't shrink when pressed; scaling every button makes the screen feel springy.

Buttons, triggers, toggles, nav rows, checkboxes and radios change fill on `:active`. Press scale only
where the motion is the component's point (hold or slide actions, expanding controls, card stacks).

### 24. Transition named properties, briefly

`transition-all` animates layout you didn't mean to, and slow hovers feel laggy.

`transition-colors` or `transition-[box-shadow,background-color]`; `duration-150` for hover and press,
`200` for state changes, `300` for reveals; ease `cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1)`. Springs stay bounce-free:
stiffness 380–520, damping 26–42, mass 0.5–0.7.

### 25. Gate movement on reduced motion

Movement, scale and blur can make some readers ill; an opacity fade carries the same change.

`useReducedMotion()`, `motion-safe:` / `motion-reduce:`; under reduce, cross-fade instead of cutting.
Popups enter from `scale-98` plus opacity; exits are shorter than entrances.

### 26. Show a ring on keyboard focus

Keyboard users need to see where they are; a hover style doesn't help them.

`focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-ring/50` on everything interactive. `outline-none` only with
that ring. Check every change in light and dark.

### 27. Let the preview explain

A live preview already shows the look, layout and states; text that repeats it is noise.

Overview cards show the name and the preview only. Example blocks are title, preview and code, with at
most one lead-in sentence that says when to use it.

### 28. Keep descriptions to one plain sentence

A registry description is the page lede, the search text and the meta tag at once.

One sentence of 12 words or fewer, no values, lists or paths. Exact values go in the API table or a note.

### 29. Never write colon lists or stacked adjectives

"X: a, b, c and d" and "powerful, seamless" read as filler.

Say what the thing does. Drop complete, comprehensive, powerful, seamless, robust, modern, flexible.

### 30. Describe what it does, not where it came from

Copy names the job, not the projects behind it.

"Block editor", "the syntax highlighter", "desktop density". No `inspired by`, `port of` or `X-style` in
comments, copy or docs; licence notices live in one notices file. Package names stay where they are
needed: imports, dependencies, install commands.

### 31. Name template parts apart from registry items

A part file named like an item (`parts/avatar.tsx` next to the `avatar` item) collides on install and in imports.

Name parts for their job: `parts/author-avatar.tsx`, `parts/buffers.ts`.

### 32. Run the upgrade check after a theme update

The CLI adds and updates theme variables but never deletes one, so removed tokens linger.

`npx shadcn@latest add @qinyang/upgrade-check`, then `node scripts/qinyang-upgrade-check.mjs` (`--fix`
cleans the stylesheet). The design check runs it for you when it is installed.

## References

| File | Covers |
| --- | --- |
| `references/foundations.md` | Colour roles and values, accent presets, elevation, radius scale and cap, fonts and type |
| `references/components.md` | Composition, lint contracts, menus, cards, file trees, avatars, removed components |
| `references/layout.md` | Density, spacing, shells, sidebars, docs chrome |
| `references/copy.md` | Copy density, descriptions, long-form prose, naming |
| `references/icons.md` | Icon families, sizes, chips, brand marks, drawing new icons |
| `references/charts.md` | Chart palette, order, swatches, labels |
| `references/motion-a11y.md` | Springs, durations, press, reduced motion, focus, dark mode |
| `references/registry.md` | Installing, upgrading, adding items, the checks |

# Charts

## Palette

`chart-1` … `chart-8` are fixed hues from the same scales as the theme: blue, orange, violet, green, pink,
amber, cyan, gray. Step 9 everywhere, except light orange (10) and amber (11) so every series is at least
3:1 on white; display-p3 copies included.

- Series take them in order (`var(--chart-N)`, `fill-chart-N`, `bg-chart-N`); `chartColor(i)` cycles all
  eight before blending.
- The order keeps neighbours far apart in both modes, and the first pair (blue, orange) survives
  red-green colour blindness. Green and pink are never neighbours.
- Charts never use `primary` and never follow the accent preset: a neutral or green accent would collide
  with the gray or green series.
- Status colours (`success`, `warning`, `destructive`) only where the colour means a status (up/down,
  errors).

## Swatches and labels

- Legend and tooltip swatches are round dots (`ChartSwatch`), so they read the same at every radius. A
  heat-map's "Less … More" key keeps the cell shape because it is a key to the cells.
- Labels on a filled shape pick their colour from the fill's luminance (`onFill`), never fixed white.
- Numbers in axes, tooltips and legends are `tabular-nums`. Donut and gauge labels stay inside the ring.
- Grid lines are `border-subtle`; axes `muted-foreground` at `text-ui-xs`.

# Components and composition

## Composing

- Import from the installed files (`@/components/ui/<name>` or wherever `components.json` points).
- Library files own their look. In screens, a component's `className` is for layout only: margins,
  `w-full`, flex/grid placement, position. Card parts take spacing, titles take typography, buttons take
  margins and `w-full`.
- If a style is missing, use a `variant` or `size`, or style a plain wrapper `<div>`. Add a variant to the
  component only when the design needs a new treatment, in its own change.
- Writing a component: named parts with `data-slot`, variants with `cva`, `className` forwarded through
  `cn`, tokens only, radii from `--radius`, `frame-*` on its own root when children use `rounded-inner`.

## Surfaces

- Cards: `rounded-xl bg-card shadow-raised`. Two-layer cards (`<Card variant="inset">` + `<CardPanel>`: a
  tinted `p-1` frame around a raised panel) only for presented content such as demos, media, code and
  featured plans; dashboards keep the plain card. Never stack two-layer cards.
- Popups (menu, context menu, select, combobox): `rounded-2xl p-1 bg-popover shadow-surface`, rows
  `min-h-6.5 px-2 rounded-lg` (inner), separators `mx-2 my-1`. Popovers stay opaque.
- Dialogs, drawers and sheets: `rounded-3xl shadow-xl`, a plain dim backdrop (no blur), `overscroll-contain`
  on anything that scrolls. Keep a dialog mounted and drive it with `open`, so it can animate out.
- Code: static code is `CodeBlock` / `CodeGroup` with markup highlighted at build time. The streaming code
  block is only for code an agent writes or opens live.

## Menus and lists

- A label sits inside its group: `<MenuGroup><MenuLabel>…</MenuLabel>…</MenuGroup>`. The same for
  `SelectLabel` and `ComboboxLabel`. Outside a group the primitive label throws.
- File trees: folders show only the expand chevron, files show their file-type icon in the same column, so
  names at one level align. Indent per level stays narrow (a code-editor sidebar, not a document outline).
- Breadcrumbs end in plain text, no frame on the current page.
- Truncated tab or row labels show the full text in a tooltip.

## People and things

- People and workspaces are avatars (`Avatar`, image or initials, or `GeneratedAvatar` in the one
  illustrated style), round for people, `shape="rounded"` for workspaces and teams. Never a generic icon
  in an avatar slot.
- Other products' logos come from `BrandIcon` (see `icons.md`).

## Not in the library

Removed on purpose and not to be added back: novelty buttons (magnetic, metallic), decorative range
sliders, 3D carousels and tilt cards, glitch or spotlight 404 pages, prediction-market and trading
widgets, the dock, returns calendar, bracket and wheel visualisations, voice orb, thinking shimmer and
the other effect-only pieces. Prefer a plain component plus a token over a showcase effect.

# Copy

The preview explains the component. Text only covers what the preview can't show. (The same rules ship
alone as the `copy-density` skill.)

## Rules

1. **Overview cards: name and preview only.** No description on gallery or overview cards. Never write the
   colon-list pattern ("X: a, b, c and d") anywhere.
2. **The preview is the explanation.** Where a live preview is shown, text never describes what it
   already shows (layout, look, motion, states).
3. **Implementation details stay on the detail page.** Install paths, pixel values, variant lists and file
   locations never appear in cards, nav, search or ledes; they go in the page body (an example, a note,
   the API table).
4. **Example blocks are title, preview and code.** At most one lead-in sentence, and it says *when to use*
   it, never *what it is*. When the title says it, drop the sentence.
5. **No stacked adjectives.** Drop complete, comprehensive, powerful, seamless, robust, beautiful, modern,
   flexible, fully-featured, blazing.
6. **Self-check.** Any card or lede over two lines gets cut to one. Delete any sentence the preview, the
   title or the API table already says.

## Where text goes

| Surface | Allowed |
| --- | --- |
| Gallery and overview card | Name only |
| Registry `description` (CLI, nav search, page lede, `<meta>`) | One plain sentence, 12 words or fewer, what it is for; no values, lists or paths |
| Detail page example | Title, plus an optional "when to use" sentence |
| Notes, API table | What the preview can't show (keyboard, accessibility, reduced motion, edge cases) and exact values |
| Guides and changelog | Short paragraphs on what changed or what to do; no marketing |

## Rewrites

- ❌ "Buttons in six variants: default, secondary, outline, ghost, destructive and link."
  ✅ "Triggers an action or submits a form."
- ❌ "A powerful, fully accessible date picker with seamless keyboard support."
  ✅ "Picks a single date or a range."
- ❌ Example "Disabled": "A disabled button that can't be clicked." ✅ *(no sentence)*

## Wording

- Sentence case for headings, labels and buttons; product names keep their own case.
- Name the job, not the origin: "block editor", "desktop density", "the dialog primitive", "the syntax
  highlighter". Never name the projects or products behind a piece in comments, copy, demo data or
  docs, and never write `after X`, `X-style`, `X-like`, `port of`, `inspired by` or `based on`. Licence attribution lives only in the project's notices file. Package names stay where they
  are needed: imports, dependency lists, install commands, public API names.
- Labels say what happens ("Delete project", not "OK"); errors say what to do next; empty states say what
  the space is for and the one action that fills it.

## Long-form prose

Guides, changelogs, notes and blog or docs pages render inside a `typeset typeset-docs` container. Don't
hand-style headings, paragraphs and lists inside it; put `not-typeset` on components dropped into prose.

# Foundations Every value lives in the theme stylesheet (`app/globals.css` in a project that installed `@qinyang/theme`). Use the tokens below; add a new one only in its own reviewed change, with a light and a `.dark` value and an `@theme inline` mapping. ## Colour roles Values are steps of 12-step colour scales, written as hex with a display-p3 copy under `@supports (color: color(display-p3 1 1 1))`. Alpha steps stay alpha, so text, fills and borders read on any surface. | Token | Light | Dark | Use | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `background` | `#fff` | `oklch(15% 0 0)` | page | | `card` | `#fff` | `#111` | cards, tables, code, raised controls | | `popover` | `#fff` | `#222` | menus, popovers, dialogs | | `shell` | `#f6f6f6` | `#000` | app chrome behind an inset panel | | `surface-sunken` / `surface-standout` | black a1 / gray 12 | black a6 / `#222` | wells, inverted callouts | | `foreground` | gray a12 | gray a12 | text | | `muted-foreground` | gray a11 | gray a11 | secondary text, nav icons | | `fg-tertiary` / `fg-disabled` | gray a9 / a8 | same steps | meta, disabled text | | `secondary`, `muted` | gray a3 | gray a3 | **translucent** default and hover fills | | `accent` | gray a4 | gray a4 | **translucent** stronger hover / selected fill | | `border` / `border-subtle` / `border-strong`, `input` | gray a3 / a2 / a6 | same steps | hairlines, field edges | | `destructive` / `success` / `warning` | tomato 9 / green 9 / orange 9 | same | status solids; each has `-hover` (10), `-foreground`, `-subtle` (a3), `-border` (a6) | | `code` | gray 2 | gray 2 | code block background | | `chart-1` … `chart-8` | see `charts.md` | | data series | - Washes: `bg-success-subtle inset-ring inset-ring-success-border` (badges, chips, alerts). Opacity modifiers (`ring-primary/20`) are fine for one-offs. - `secondary`, `muted` and `accent` are fills, not surfaces. Anything opaque uses `bg-card`, `bg-popover` or `bg-background`. - No gradient sheens, inset highlights, text shadows or glows. ## Accent Eight roles carry the accent: `primary` (solid, step 9), `primary-hover` (10), `primary-active` (11), `primary-foreground`, `primary-subtle` (a3), `primary-subtle-hover` (a4), `primary-border` (a6) and `ring` (a8 light, a9 dark, used at `/50`). The default is blue `#0090ff`. Presets (neutral, green, orange, rose, violet) are `html[data-accent="…"]` blocks that swap the eight on the same steps of their own scale; neutral is the inverted black/white solid. Each ships as a `theme-` registry item. Filled controls hover to `bg-primary-hover`; text on any solid is its `*-foreground`. Charts never follow the accent. ## Elevation | Level | Tailwind | Named tokens | Use | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | border | `shadow-xs` | `shadow-chip`, `shadow-pressed` | keys, small chips | | default | `shadow-sm` | `shadow-raised` → `hover:shadow-raised-hover` | resting controls, cards, tables, code | | lg | `shadow-md`, `shadow-lg` | `shadow-surface` | popovers, menus, floating panels | | xl | `shadow-xl` | | dialogs, alert dialogs, drawers, sheets, command palette | | inset | | `shadow-well` | fields and tracks | | primary | | `shadow-primary` | filled primary | Each level includes its hairline (a 0.5–1px ring), so don't add a CSS border to a shadowed surface. Dark elevation is an inset white hairline plus deeper drops. Hover on rows, menu items, ghost and outline buttons and nav is a fill (`bg-secondary`), not a ring. App chrome: `bg-shell` with the `shell-inset` utility (0.5px hairline, `rounded-shell`, 3px gap). ## Radius `--radius` is 0.5rem. Tokens are multiples of it, clamped at `--radius-max` (1rem): | Token | × | Default | Use | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `rounded-xs` (`2xs`) | 0.25 | 2px | carets, tiny marks | | `rounded-sm` | 0.5 | 4px | xs buttons, checkboxes | | `rounded-md` | 0.75 | 6px | tab indicators in a `p-0.5` list | | `rounded-lg` | 1 | 8px | buttons, inputs, triggers, tab lists, menu and select rows | | `rounded-xl` | 1.25 | 10px | cards, tables, code blocks | | `rounded-2xl` | 1.5 | 12px | menus and popups (`p-1`, rows 12 − 4 = 8px), two-layer inset cards | | `rounded-3xl` | 2 | 16px | containers holding controls 8px in (prompt bars, composers, rails), dialogs | | `rounded-shell` | 1.5 | 12px | the rail's inset panel | | `rounded-4xl`, `rounded-5xl` | | 16px | old names at the cap; don't use | Presets: none 0, sm 0.375rem, default 0.5rem, lg 0.625rem, xl 0.875rem; a custom value goes up to 1rem. `html[data-radius="…"]` or an inline `--radius` on `` switches them. ### Concentric nesting Declare the container with `frame-*` and the child follows it: ```tsx
{/* 12px, 4px in */}
…
{/* 12 − 4 = 8px */}
``` | Utility | On | Does | | --- | --- | --- | | `frame-{sm…3xl,shell}` | container | its radius; publishes radius − inset to descendants | | `frame-p-{n}` | container | padding on all sides and the inset used in the maths | | `frame-inset-{n}` | container | only the inset (gap from a wrapper, asymmetric padding) | | `frame-border` | container | counts a 1px border into the inset | | `rounded-inner`, `rounded-{t,b,s,e}-inner` | child | frame radius − inset (min 2px); `rounded-lg` outside any frame | | `frame-inner` | padded child | takes the inner radius and publishes its own (level 2). Never with `rounded-inner` on the same element | | `rounded-inner-{token}` | child | concentric in a frame, `{token}` outside one | | `rounded-inner-or-{token}` | child | inner radius when usable, else `{token}` capped at `rounded-sm` | When it applies: insets of 8px or less are always concentric. If radius − inset would be under 4px the container is too loose: the child keeps its own token (or tighten the padding). For 9–15px insets, surfaces (rows, panels, wells, media) stay concentric; self-contained controls keep their token. A child is never rounder than its container. Two levels are supported; a third computes its value. ## Type Inter Variable (`ss03`) → Noto Sans SC → system for UI; JetBrains Mono → system mono for code, keys and terminals; Newsreader → Noto Serif SC only in the reading preset. Letter spacing normal. Self-hosted through the `fonts` item; the theme falls back to system fonts without it. | Size | px | Use | | --- | --- | --- | | `text-ui-2xs` | 10 | tiny meta | | `text-ui-xs` | 11 | meta, shortcuts, counts | | `text-ui-sm` | 12 | captions, badges, small controls, tooltips | | `text-ui` | 13 | default UI: buttons, inputs, menus, nav, body inside components | | `text-ui-lg` | 14 | lg controls, card titles | Tailwind's `text-sm`–`text-2xl` are for reading copy and page or section headings; `text-3xl`+ only for heroes. Weights: 400, 450 (`font-semimedium`), 500, 600, 700. Titles semibold (`tracking-tight` only from `text-xl`), labels and buttons medium, secondary text `text-muted-foreground`. `text-balance` on headings, `text-pretty` on paragraphs, `tabular-nums` on numbers that change or align. Inline code in prose sits a little smaller than the text around it (`0.85em`–`0.9em`).

# Icons and brand marks

All glyphs come from the house set (`@qinyang/icons`, installed as `components/icons.tsx`), never another
icon package or an ad-hoc SVG. Drawing new glyphs is the `puffy-icons` skill
(`npx skills add QinYangWang/ui --skill puffy-icons`); it covers the grids, primitives and preview script
for every style.

## Styles

One file, three styles with the same exports: rounded (default, 24×24, 1.75px strokes), puffy (18×18 soft
filled shapes) and outline (the puffy shapes as 1.6px outlines). Switch a project with
`npx shadcn@latest add <site>/r/icons-puffy.json --overwrite` (or `icons-outline.json`, `icons.json`).
Check a new icon in every style at 14px.

## Families

- **Solid**: filled silhouettes with knockouts (`HomeIcon`, `BotIcon`, `SettingsIcon`, `InboxIcon`,
  `CalendarDaysIcon`, `ServerIcon`, `TerminalSquareIcon`).
- **Line / ring**: open glyphs and outlined objects (chevrons, arrows, check, x, search, `MailIcon`,
  `CalendarIcon`, `InfoIcon`, `ClockIcon`).
- A set shown side by side (nav list, rail, dock, tab bar, palette group, a feed of cards) uses one family.
  Navigation uses solid: `InboxIcon` not `MailIcon`, `CalendarDaysIcon` not `CalendarIcon`,
  `TerminalSquareIcon` not `TerminalIcon`. Line glyphs are for controls.

## Sizes and colour

| Context | Size | Colour | Frame |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Nav item, rail, command palette | 16px | `text-muted-foreground`, active `text-foreground` | bare |
| Inline in a button, badge or meta row | the control sets it | inherits | bare |
| Card, header, notification or alert icon | the chip sets it | chip tone | `IconChip` |
| Brand mark in a header | 22px | `text-foreground` | bare |

`IconChip` sizes `sm` 24 / `default` 32 / `lg` 40 / `xl` 48; tones neutral, primary, success, warning,
destructive, solid. One size per list. Chips are squircles, never circles (circles are avatars and status
dots). On an icon, `className` takes size, layout, a token colour, opacity and motion only. Inline icons
align with the first line of text.

## Brand marks

Other products' logos (sign-in providers, integrations, agents, languages) use
`<BrandIcon icon={siGithub} />` from `@qinyang/brand-icon`, with one named import per logo (never
`import *` or a lookup by slug). `color="brand"` where the logo is the content (a list of apps), the
default `current` in toolbars and nav. Brands the package leaves out get a neutral icon from the set,
never a redrawn mark.

## Not icons

Progress rings, chart geometry and sparklines, illustration artwork and animated checkmarks stay
hand-drawn SVG inside their components.

# Layout and density

## Density

| Thing | Size |
| --- | --- |
| Button | `h-8` default, `sm` `h-7`, `xs`/`icon-xs` `h-6`, `lg` `h-9`; `icon` 32, `icon-sm` 28 |
| Input, select and combobox trigger | `h-8` (`sm` `h-7`), `px-2.5` |
| Menu, select and combobox row | `min-h-6.5` (26px), `px-2`, popup `p-1` |
| Tooltip | `px-2 py-1 text-ui-sm` |
| Sidebar row | `h-8` (sub rows `h-7`), `text-ui`, muted icons, hover `bg-secondary`, active `bg-foreground/6` |
| Checkbox, radio | 16px; switch 32×20 |
| Disabled | `opacity-64` |

Use the component's `size` prop, not heights on the instance.

## Spacing

4px grid. Icon + label `gap-1.5`–`gap-2`; control groups `gap-2`–`gap-3`; card padding `p-4`–`p-6`;
stacked sections `gap-6`–`gap-10`. Related text sits closer together than the content it belongs to
(title and description `gap-1`, sections `gap-6`). Space goes on the parent (`gap`) or as margin on the
child, never as padding added to a component. Vertical padding around text is a little smaller than
horizontal (line height adds the rest).

## Shells

- Apps: a `bg-shell` window with the content in a `shell-inset` panel (hairline, `rounded-shell`, 3px
  gap). Internal dividers are `border-border`.
- Sidebar and header align: the collapse button, back/forward and the right sidebar's buttons sit on one
  row height; the sidebar's text column starts at the header brand's left edge.
- Navigation text starts on one left edge: section labels (`text-ui` semibold), group labels
  (`text-ui-sm` medium muted, `mt-2` above) and rows all put text on the same line, no indent and no guide
  line; chevrons on the right. Active row = fill plus an optional 2px bar in the gutter.
- Documentation chrome is one white surface split by hairlines (sticky `h-12` header with `border-b`,
  text-only sidebar rows, an "On this page" rail from `xl`), not an app shell.

## Scrolling

Scrollable panels use `ScrollArea` so the bar stays inside the frame and spans the scroll range; sticky
headers inside them separate with `border-b`, not a shadow. Collapsing content keeps its size while it
animates closed.

## Responsive

Check every screen at 390, 768 and 1024px wide and in right-to-left. Toolbars collapse labels to icons
(with tooltips) before they wrap; tables scroll horizontally inside their frame.

# Motion, accessibility and themes

## Motion

- Springs are bounce-free and close to critically damped: `{ type: "spring", stiffness: 380–520,
  damping: 26–42, mass: 0.5–0.7 }` (420/38/0.6 for settles, 500/30 for snappy toggles). Icon cross-fades:
  `{ type: "spring", duration: 0.3, bounce: 0 }`.
- CSS: `duration-150` for press, hover and other high-frequency changes, `duration-200` for state changes,
  `duration-300` for reveals and panels; easing `cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1)` (`EASE = [0.22, 1, 0.36, 1]`).
  The overshoot curve `cubic-bezier(0.34,1.56,0.64,1)` only for playful pops.
- Transition named properties (`transition-colors`, `transition-[box-shadow,background-color,color]`,
  `transition-transform`), never `transition-all`. `will-change` only for a stutter you saw, naming the
  property.
- Staggered entrances 100ms apart (opacity + 4px blur + 12px rise, 300ms ease-out); exits shorter (150ms).
  `initial={false}` on `AnimatePresence` state swaps. Popups enter from `scale-98` plus opacity.
- **No press scale on standard controls** (buttons, triggers, toggles, nav rows, checkboxes, radios):
  they answer with a fill change. A press scale (to `0.96` over 150ms) stays only where the motion is the
  component's point, and a disabled control never scales.
- Collapsing content keeps its size while it closes, so text doesn't reflow mid-animation.

## Reduced motion

Every movement, scale or blur is gated (`useReducedMotion()`, `motion-safe:`, `motion-reduce:`). Under
reduce, cross-fade opacity instead of cutting the change. Loops (spinners, marquees, shimmers) slow down or
stop.

## Focus and keyboard

- `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-ring/50` on every interactive element; `outline-none` only
  together with that ring. Inside scroll frames use `focus-visible:ring-inset`.
- Every control has an accessible name (visible label, `aria-label` on icon-only buttons, a `label` on
  sliders). Menus, selects, tabs and trees keep their primitive's keyboard model.
- Hotkeys show their shortcut in a `Kbd`; one listener per shortcut, not one per instance.

## Light and dark

Every change must look right with and without `.dark` on `<html>`. Use tokens, not `dark:` overrides with
palette colours. Check both themes, an accent preset and the smallest and largest radius before you
finish.

# Registry, CLI and upgrades

## Installing

Add the namespace to `components.json`, then install the theme and any item:

```json
{ "registries": { "@qinyang": "https://qinyangwang.github.io/ui/r/{name}.json" } }
```

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @qinyang/theme
npx shadcn@latest add @qinyang/button @qinyang/menu
npx shadcn@latest view @qinyang/card        # inspect before installing
```

Templates install whole screens (`@qinyang/saas`, `@qinyang/agent-workspace`, `@qinyang/docs`,
`@qinyang/blog`, `@qinyang/vscode`). Components list the icon set as a dependency: when the CLI asks to
overwrite `components/icons.tsx`, answer no to keep your icon style.

## This skill

```bash
npx skills add QinYangWang/ui --skill qinyang-design   # agent skill (rules, references, checks)
npx shadcn@latest add @qinyang/design-skill            # same files through the shadcn CLI
```

The registry copy lands in `.agents/skills/qinyang-design/` at the project root, also in projects with `src/`.
Run the check from the project root:
`node .agents/skills/qinyang-design/scripts/check.mjs`.

## Upgrading

The CLI merges a newer theme into your stylesheet: it adds and updates variables but never deletes one.
After a theme update:

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @qinyang/theme --overwrite
npx shadcn@latest add @qinyang/upgrade-check
node scripts/qinyang-upgrade-check.mjs          # report; exit 1 when something needs fixing
node scripts/qinyang-upgrade-check.mjs --fix    # cleans the stylesheet, then reports only what is left
```

It finds the removed accent ramp, broken wide-gamut overrides, `@property` rules left by theme 2.2 and earlier
(the CLI appended a copy on every reinstall; theme 2.3 ships none, so reinstalls are idempotent), themes without
the 16px cap or with `--radius` above 1rem, and source that still uses removed classes. The design check
runs it when it is installed.

## Adding an item (library maintainers)

1. Component in `registry/<style>/ui/<name>.tsx` (or `blocks/<name>/`), named parts with `data-slot`,
   variants with `cva`, `className` through `cn`.
2. One demo per item, written as a consumer (tokens only, layout classes on components).
3. The `registry.json` entry: `name`, `type`, `title`, a one-sentence `description` (12 words or fewer),
   `dependencies`, `registryDependencies` (`@qinyang/theme`, `@qinyang/icons`, `@qinyang/icon-chip` …),
   `files`, `meta.category`.
4. Template parts are named for their job and never share a name with a registry item.
5. Run the linter, the type check, this skill's check, and rebuild the registry. After changing radii or
   padding on nested surfaces, run the runtime radius audit (or `scripts/radius-probe.js` on the page).

## The checks

| Check | Catches | Run |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `scripts/check.mjs` | Static rules (see `--list`) | `node <skill>/scripts/check.mjs [paths]` |
| `scripts/radius-probe.js` | Nested radii as rendered, including open menus and hovered rows | paste in the console on the page |
| Upgrade check | Stale theme leftovers | `node scripts/qinyang-upgrade-check.mjs` |
| Linter (`@shadcn/lint` + the concentric rule) | Restyles, raw colours, arbitrary values | `eslint .` |

Allow-list an intentional finding in `qinyang-design.config.json` with a reason:

```json
{ "allow": [{ "rule": "type-scale", "file": "components/card-art.tsx", "reason": "card artwork" }] }
```

or on one line with a comment `design-check-ignore <rule> -- <reason>` above it.
